{{short description|American physicist and professor}}
'''Robert T. Siegel''' (1928–2000) graduated from Carnegie Tech (now [[Carnegie Mellon University]]) in 1948, and attained a [[D.Sc]] in 1952. He was [[professor]] of [[physics]] at the [[College of William and Mary]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Robert T. Siegel Oral History|url=https://digitalarchive.wm.edu/handle/10288/5472|publisher=College of William & Mary|accessdate=12 September 2013}}</ref> from 1963 to 1998, and director of the [[Space Radiation Effects Laboratory]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Siegel|first=Robert|title=Space Radiation Effects Laboratory|url=https://archive.org/details/nasa_techdoc_20040075026|publisher=College of William and Mary|accessdate=12 September 2013}}</ref> located on the site where the [[Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility]] would later be built, from its construction in 1964–65 to its decommissioning in 1980.
